The bug report says that with wide bounds (like near Double.MAX_VALUE), the optimizer calls the fitness function with NaN parameters. The test case sets very large bounds near half of Double.MAX_VALUE and expects a NumberIsTooLargeException. The reported bug is that NaN values appear in parameters passed to the fitness function instead.

This suggests the problem occurs during the parameter normalization / denormalization in the encoding/decoding steps inside CMAESOptimizer or its base classes. Particularly, when the difference between the bounds is huge, computing a normalized value can lead to overflow and result in NaN.

I attempted to get the code for CMAESOptimizer.optimize but it has multiple overrides. Likely the normalization logic is in a base class such as BaseAbstractMultivariateSimpleBoundsOptimizer or CMAESOptimizer itself in their encode/decode or optimize methods. We need to see these methods to confirm how normalization is done (divide by range between bounds) and how large ranges could produce NaN.

Next, I will look for encode and decode methods in CMAESOptimizer or base classes related to parameter normalization. This will help verify if large differences produce NaN leading to this failure symptom.
